purpose: Teach: 取りあえず/なかには/ちらほら/うかがっ/食え/何れ/ほったらかし/大概

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは取りあえず茶を出されたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father would be served tea straightaway.
lines.style: Distant, almost to himself. Slow cadence—not rushing to fill silence. Warm but untethered, like he's watching the memory more than speaking it. Gentle fade on the period.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、ご友人のなかには商人もいらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, Grandfather—you had merchants among your friends too, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Soft affirmation with a gentle tilt of curiosity. Not quite a question, more an invitation to keep going. Warm patience. The slight lilt on 'dear' brings him back to the room with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、桜がちらほら咲いた朝を覚えてるぞ
lines.en: Gran, I remember a spring morning when I was young—cherry blossoms scattered across it.
lines.style: Slower still. The image arrives before the words. Breathing space before 'cherry blossoms.' Tender, half-lost in the detail. Voice trails into the quiet of that particular dawn.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫さんのお話を熱心にうかがってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandfather, you used to listen so carefully when the grandchildren would tell you things, didn't you?
lines.style: Gentle reaffirmation, almost protective of the memory. She's guiding him gently deeper, not away. Warm, conspiratorial—just the two of them holding this. Slight pause before 'didn't you, dear?'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「腹がへったら食えよ」と仰ったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father once told me, 'If you're hungry, eat.'
lines.style: A small exhale before the quote, like he can hear the voice again. The quoted words are direct, uncomplicated—how his father said them. Then a beat after, returning to the memory. Not sad, just present with it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、何れ天国でまた会いましょうね、あなた
lines.en: Grandfather, we'll see each other again in heaven someday, won't we, dear?
lines.style: Not tentative—certain, but tender. A hand reaching across time and space. No performance, just the thing said that needed saying. Warm on 'dear,' like she's holding his hand in the words.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんは仕事をほったらかしになさらなかったぞ
lines.en: Gran, Father never neglected his work.
lines.style: Short, definitive—a fact stated with quiet conviction. But not hard. The pride in it sits underneath, unperformed. A man describing another man he knew well. Settles on the period.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、大概、夕食前に新聞をお読みになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandfather, he used to read the newspaper before dinner most evenings, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: A small smile in the voice. She's confirming the dailiness, the ritual of him. Intimate and close—these small beautiful repetitions. Warmth at the end, drawing him near. A gentle closing.
